facts.text: Taiwanese opera (gezaixi) troupes began in Yilan County in the early 20th century; Yilan is known as its birthplace.
Taiwanese opera is considered one of the few Han art forms that developed locally in Taiwan.
Early performers improvised in town plazas, and shows were staged outdoors during temple festivals.
Troupes still perform on the temple circuit, and outdoor shows involve more interaction between actors and the audience than big theater productions.
Improvised dialogue is a central part of the entertainment in Taiwanese opera.
Actresses playing male characters became a tradition in Taiwanese opera; the young male lead roles are known as xiaosheng.
Some newer troupes add modern elements, such as rock songs and costumes inspired by manga and cosplay.
Audiences at many Taiwanese opera performances today are mainly older people, and troupes hope to reach younger viewers.
